pool.text: Spanish cavalryman Gabriel Moraga surveyed and named the Río del Santísimo Sacramento river.
Mexican governor Juan Bautista Alvarado granted the responsibility of colonizing the Sacramento Valley.
The waterfront developed by Sutter began to be developed and incorporated as the city.
The city became the permanent state capital and started building a new capitol.
Voters adopted the city charter that currently guides the municipal government operations.
Sacramento voters approved the creation of the utility district known as SMUD.
A judge ordered Pacific Gas and Electric to transfer the electric distribution system.
Sacramento State was founded as Sacramento State College in the local area.
The merger of the City of North Sacramento substantially increased the population numbers.
Sacramento Country Day School opened and offered citizens an independent school.
Ronald Reagan became the last Governor of California to live permanently here.
The Arbor Day Foundation designated the municipality as a City of Trees.
Computer store owner Hugh Scrutton was killed by a bomb left outside.
Masjid Annur, an Islamic school in Sacramento, was founded.
Capitol Casino opened in downtown and is home to several card games.
The airport on the former McClellan Air Force Base site transferred to Sacramento County.
The Wells Fargo Pavilion was built atop the old Music Circus tent foundations.
The city of West Sacramento took responsibility for managing the local port.
Sacramento was designated as a Silver Level Bicycle Friendly Community.
The municipality started the marketing campaign known as America's Farm-to-Fork Capital.
